mu = (u - tan_s[k]) / (tan_s[k+1] - tan_s[k])

Found by a MONOTONE MERGE SCAN: one pointer walks forward
as q advances, O(M + Mp) per line rather than O(Mp log M).
Both sequences are sorted, so the pointer never goes back." style="text;html=1;strokeColor=none;fillColor=none;align=center;verticalAlign=middle;fontSize=11;fontFamily=Helvetica;" vertex="1" parent="1"><mxGeometry x="700" y="236" width="436" height="116" as="geometry" /></mxCell><mxCell id="m2" value="The KERNEL is identical to range -- same 2-tap blend, same 32-tap sinc variant. Only the way
k and mu are FOUND differs. That is why one gather core can serve both passes, and why the
interpolator upgrade applies to both." style="text;html=1;strokeColor=none;fillColor=none;align=center;verticalAlign=middle;fontSize=11;fontFamily=Helvetica;" vertex="1" parent="1"><mxGeometry x="24" y="380" width="640" height="60" as="geometry" /></mxCell><mxCell id="e0" value="" style="edgeStyle=orthogonalEdgeStyle;rounded=1;html=1;fontSize=11;strokeColor=#444444;dashed=1;" edge="1" parent="1" source="k0" target="qt"><mxGeometry relative="1" as="geometry" /></mxCell><mxCell id="e1" value="" style="edgeStyle=orthogonalEdgeStyle;rounded=1;html=1;fontSize=11;strokeColor=#444444;dashed=1;" edge="1" parent="1" source="k1" target="qt"><mxGeometry relative="1" as="geometry" /></mxCell></root></mxGraphModel></diagram></mxfile>
svg.text: After the corner-turn each RANGE BIN is a row of pulses. The source abscissa is tan(phi) of each pulse -- and the
platform does not fly at constant angular rate, so these are NOT evenly spaced. That is the one structural difference from range.
unevenly spaced -- the gaps differ, so the bracket cannot be computed by division
Found by a MONOTONE MERGE SCAN: one pointer walks forward
as q advances, O(M + Mp) per line rather than O(Mp log M).
Both sequences are sorted, so the pointer never goes back.
The KERNEL is identical to range -- same 2-tap blend, same 32-tap sinc variant. Only the way
